newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Royale Belge positive on 1997 outlook.
newsitem.headline: Royale Belge positive on 1997 outlook.

text.p: Belgian insurer Royale Belge SA is confident its long-term objectives of achieving growth in results and dividend will be fulfilled in 1997, chief executive officer Jean-Pierre Gerard said on Thursday.

"In 1997 our objective is to achieve regular growth versus the 7.1 billion francs current profit we achieved in 1996. Growth of 500 million to one billion francs is reasonable and should be able to be attained," he told a news conference on 1996 earnings.

Royale Belge group net profit rose to 11.3 billion francs in 1996 from 6.2 billion in 1995, boosted by a 4.2 billion franc extraordinary gain on the sale of shares in Belgian holding company Tractebel SA.
Current profit was therefore 7.1 billion francs, the group, which is controlled jointly by France's AXA-UAP and Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, said.
Gerard said AXA-UAP had a long-term objective of achieving a return on equity (ROE) as a group as a whole of 15 percent by 2000.
Royale Belge's ROE, excluding the capital gain on the sale of Tractebel shares, at the end of 1996 was 12.6 percent. He noted that methods of calculating ROE vary from company to company.
